hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input so edge 4 is dead and upgrading it gives almost no gain.
Restoring a direct input-to-output path where none existed gives a much larger gain than replacing an existing op with a skip.
Deleting the strong direct 3x3 conv loses far more accuracy than deleting a weaker op.
Removing a 3x3 conv on the input edge destroys more capacity than removing a skip or pool.
When the direct edge 3 is a parameter-free pool, adding a conv on edge 0 yields much smaller gains.
Replacing a pooling op with a 3x3 conv gives a smaller gain than replacing a 1x1 conv, skip or none.
Replacing an avg-pool with a 3x3 conv gives a smaller gain than replacing a 1x1 conv, skip or none.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a pool on edge 2 hurts a lot, whereas replacing weaker ops is roughly neutral or helpful.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a skip on the output edge costs substantial accuracy compared to swapping weaker ops.
Upgrading edge 4 helps much less when edge 3 is a pool, since the cell's other paths then contribute little.
